commitResults.messageTitle: Remove the unused bulk tag parser
commitResults.messageBody:
`ParserUtil.parseTags` has no production callers, so the only things it
serves are its own tests. The commands that read tags take them one
value at a time through the problem collector, which reports every
value it refuses instead of stopping at the first.

Let's remove the unused API, the imports it needed and the tests that
existed only to cover it. `parseTag`, which the collector uses, stays.

commitResults.messageTitle: Parse optional edit fields through the collector
commitResults.messageBody:
The optional email and NUS Student ID of an edit are read by a try
block that catches the parse failure and records it by hand. The
problem collector already does that, and every other field of the
command is read through it.

Let's collect the parsed value instead of catching the failure here.
The setter is reached only when the collector accepted the value, so a
rejected one leaves the descriptor as it was.

commitResults.messageTitle: Cover the values the collector keeps
commitResults.messageBody:
The collector keeps the values it accepts in a set, so the same tag
named twice is one tag. Nothing said so, and the bulk parser it
replaced had no test for it either.

Let's cover a value given twice, and check that naming a tag twice in
an edit asks for one tag rather than two copies of it.

commitResults.messageTitle: Make the overflow test exercise a positive index
commitResults.messageBody:
The test for an index that does not fit adds one to `Integer.MAX_VALUE`
as an int, so the addition wraps around and the parser is handed
"-2147483648". It refuses that because it looks negative, not because
it is out of range, so the boundary the test names is never reached.

Let's add one as a long, so the parser is handed "2147483648", and
check that the largest index it accepts is the one below it. Zero and
negative indexes keep a test of their own, so a mistake in one is not
hidden by another.

commitResults.messageTitle: Keep the utility classes from being built
commitResults.messageBody:
`Messages` and `StringUtil` hold nothing but static members, and
neither declares a constructor. Java gives each a public one all the
same, so both can be built by anyone who misreads them, and the
constructor no test calls counts against the coverage we report.

Let's declare a private constructor in each, the way `UiText` does.
JaCoCo leaves a private empty constructor out of its report, so the
three missed instructions each class showed are gone rather than
moved.

The UG, the EditCommandParser Javadoc and the usage text say a
digit-leading ID is named through --id, but for edit --id sets the
replacement ID and never picks the student, so a student whose ID
starts with a digit cannot be edited by ID at all. The DG manual test
also runs edit 1 -p without a value, which is refused before it can
identify anyone.

Let's state that only a letter-first ID is an edit target, give the DG
comparison a complete command, tighten the unknown-ID wording that
showed two full stops, and pin both refusals in the parser test.

does not say an NUS Student ID is also a target or why this one is
not.

in the parser tests.

commitResults.messageTitle: Spell the overflow index out instead of adding it
commitResults.messageBody:
The test that an index which does not fit is refused built its input by
adding one to `Integer.MAX_VALUE` as a long, and then checked its own
arithmetic. The boundary is easier to read written out, and a written
value cannot wrap around and turn back into the negative index the
test used to pass on.

Let's spell the first index that does not fit out, and keep the comment
that explains the trap for the next reader.

commitResults.messageBody:
The Non-Functional Requirements section in the Developer Guide still
contains placeholder items from AddressBook-Level 3. These placeholders
are untestable, use generic terminology, and omit the technical
constraints defined by the project requirements.

Let's replace the placeholders with scoped non-functional requirements
tailored to TAB, specifying operating environment, portability,
concurrency, capacity, latency benchmarks, typing efficiency, and
display scaling constraints, while explicitly linking each to its
corresponding course constraint.

Enforce exit, delete, start-up and offline tests
commitResults.messageBody:
The test suite lacks coverage for several core non-functional and
command contracts specified in the Developer Guide. Exit and delete
commands miss boundary checks, parsing variations and model mutation
assertions. Application start-up fallbacks for missing or corrupted
data and preferences are untested, while multi-session persistence of
deletions and window settings has no end-to-end exercise. In addition,
keyboard-only execution and offline local storage requirements are not
explicitly verified.

Let's add test cases to cover exit and delete commands, verify start-up
initialization under missing and corrupted files, enforce data
persistence across multiple sessions, and assert keyboard-only and
offline operation contracts.

Reject arguments to commands that take none
commitResults.messageBody:
Commands without parameters ignore extra text, so a mistyped clear
can delete records and a mistyped exit can close the application.

Let's reject unexpected arguments with specific feedback and verify
that rejected commands preserve the filtered list and saved data.

commitResults.messageTitle: Document rejection of unexpected command arguments
commitResults.messageBody:
The guides describe extra arguments as ignored, which no longer
matches the safeguards on commands that take no parameters.

Let's explain the rejection feedback and whitespace behavior, and
add manual checks for preserved display and storage state.

commitResults.messageTitle: Distinguish clearing an email from leaving it alone
commitResults.messageBody:
An absent email in an edit descriptor means leave the email alone,
so the command cannot remove an address without removing the record.

Let's retain explicit email edit intent, including a null replacement,
and preserve that intent through copies, equality, and execution.

commitResults.messageTitle: Allow an explicitly empty email in edit commands
commitResults.messageBody:
Edit commands reject an empty email even when the user deliberately
supplies an empty quoted value to remove a mistaken address.

Let's accept -e "" as an email clear, keep bare and malformed values
as errors, and verify that clears survive saving and reloading.

commitResults.messageTitle: Document email clearing and its manual checks
commitResults.messageBody:
The guides describe a mistaken email as impossible to remove and do
not explain the difference between an omitted and cleared address.

Let's document explicit email clearing, the required-field boundary,
and manual checks for unchanged details and persistence.

commitResults.messageTitle: Require confirmation before clearing all records
commitResults.messageBody:
A single clear command deletes every student immediately, so a
mistyped command can remove a semester of records without warning.

Let's show the full record count and require a yes reply before
clearing and saving. Cancellation and invalid replies keep the book
and its saved file intact, and empty books need no confirmation.

commitResults.messageTitle: Verify cancellation leaves saved data untouched
commitResults.messageBody:
The confirmation flow must protect every record, including hidden
students, without rewriting the JSON file when the user cancels.

Let's check the whole-book count, reply variants, unchanged filtered
state and JSON bytes, and the absence of any storage write.

commitResults.messageTitle: Cover confirmation replies and empty student books
commitResults.messageBody:
Mistyped replies must not run another command or write data, while
confirmation must clear hidden students as well as visible ones.

Let's cover invalid input, repeated replies, case and whitespace
variants, and empty books with and without an existing data file.

commitResults.messageTitle: Check confirmation through the command line UI
commitResults.messageBody:
The confirmation prompt must remain usable from the keyboard and
connect the visible reply to the protected data on disk.

Let's exercise the Enter action through the real window, checking
prompt feedback, cancellation, confirmation, and retained input focus.

commitResults.messageTitle: Document the clear confirmation flow
commitResults.messageBody:
The guides describe clear as immediate deletion and manual checks
assume that one command is enough to remove all records.

Let's explain the prompt, replies, cancellation, and empty-book
behavior, and update manual tests to verify protected saved data.

commitResults.messageTitle: Cover non-email edits in descriptor checks
commitResults.messageBody:
The email intent change also affects how a descriptor recognizes
edits to other fields, but those paths lack direct regression checks.

Let's verify that name, phone, and tag edits still count as changes
when the email is left untouched.

commitResults.messageTitle: Place email checks beside successful commands
commitResults.messageBody:
The email persistence and unexpected-argument tests occupy the same
insertion point, creating a conflict between otherwise independent
issue branches.

Let's keep the email lifecycle checks beside the successful command
cases so each PR can merge without resolving an unrelated test hunk.

commitResults.messageTitle: Use a concise y/N prompt with exact reply aliases
commitResults.messageBody:
The clear prompt repeats instructions familiar to the target audience
and rejects the usual single-letter replies. Its default is unclear.

Let's show a concise y/N prompt, accept only y/yes and n/no ignoring
case and surrounding whitespace, and cancel on an empty reply. Words
that merely begin with either letter remain invalid.

commitResults.messageTitle: Document exact y/N replies and default cancellation
commitResults.messageBody:
The guides and screenshot describe a verbose yes/no prompt and do
not explain the concise prompt or its default cancellation behavior.

Let's document the exact reply aliases and empty Enter, update the
manual checks, and show the new one-line prompt in the PR screenshot.

commitResults.messageTitle: Overload parsing for commands with no arguments
commitResults.messageBody:
Commands with no arguments use a separately named helper, although
it performs the same command-parsing responsibility as the entry
point. This makes related parsing paths read differently.

Let's express their shared validation as a parseCommand overload and
document the dispatch while preserving the existing safeguards.

commitResults.messageTitle: Restore the explicit no-argument parsing helper
commitResults.messageBody:
The overload shares its name with the full-input parser even though
it only validates arguments for an already-created command. This
hides the narrower purpose at its call sites.

Let's restore parseNoArgumentCommand and the matching guide wording
so the restriction is explicit, while keeping the existing safeguards.

This reverts commit 68497d76fd35f484e8434d841017c9ed0f4824eb.

commitResults.messageTitle: Make email clearing explicit with Optional values
commitResults.messageBody:
An email setter accepts null to mean clear, and parser failures also
produce null. The two intentions are easy to confuse, while copying
an edit bypasses the APIs used by other fields.

Let's use Optional for the descriptor email, provide clearEmail, and
require a real address in setEmail. Copies use the same operations,
and parsing records rejected values without assigning a null email.

commitResults.messageTitle: Explain optional email edits without obsolete syntax
commitResults.messageBody:
The guide describes null as the signal for clearing an email and
compares tag clearing with an obsolete command syntax. Neither helps
a reader understand the explicit edit API.

Let's describe the three email edit states, the separate clear and
set operations, and the existing model and storage boundary.

commitResults.messageTitle: Require explicit confirmation state from Logic
commitResults.messageBody:
The default confirmation state lets a Logic implementation silently
inherit false, which can suppress empty replies even when a request is
pending. Only the test stub needs a fixed false response.

Let's require every implementation to state whether confirmation is
pending and make the stub's response explicit.

commitResults.messageTitle: Represent pending clear requests with Optional
commitResults.messageBody:
A nullable clear request makes absence implicit, and handling it inside
normal command execution adds nested conditions. Both make the
confirmation lifecycle harder to follow.

Let's represent absence explicitly and give clear requests a separate
handler while preserving cancellation, validation and save behavior.

commitResults.messageTitle: Clarify and test mixed-case confirmation replies
commitResults.messageBody:
Confirmation accepts replies without regard to case, but the tests
sample only a few capitalizations and the command summary does not
state the rule.

Let's cover every capitalization of yes and no and show mixed-case
examples in the User Guide so acceptance is clear to readers.

commitResults.messageTitle: Simplify validated email assignment
commitResults.messageBody:
The email parser uses a result-producing callback only for its setter
side effect and discards the result. The setter also checks for null
before a factory that already rejects it, obscuring simple behavior.

Let's assign validated email values directly, collect parse failures
explicitly, and keep only the necessary null rejection.

commitResults.messageTitle: Trim confirmation replies without backtracking
commitResults.messageBody:
The trailing-whitespace regex repeatedly scans internal space runs
that cannot match at the end of a reply. A large paste can therefore
block the UI for much longer than its length warrants.

Let's trim from the ends using the command parser's whitespace rules
and cover long invalid and whitespace-only replies without data writes.

commitResults.messageTitle: Report a missing clear request as command feedback
commitResults.messageBody:
The confirmation handler uses an unchecked exception if its request
is unexpectedly absent. The normal guard prevents that state, but an
inconsistent confirmation indicator would bypass normal UI feedback.

Let's return a command error with a recovery instruction instead and
verify that no records or saved data change in this failure case.

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject unexpected arguments to no-argument commands #148 (#178)
commitResults.messageBody:
Commands that take no arguments silently ignore extra input, so a
mistyped clear command can delete student records.

Let's reject unexpected arguments before execution or saving, accept
whitespace-only arguments, and explain the offending input clearly.
Update the guides and manual checks to match the safeguards.

Fixes #148

Validation: ./gradlew check coverage passes on the branch and with
all three issue branches combined. Tests verify unchanged records,
filters and saved JSON after rejected commands.

commitResults.messageTitle: Allow an email to be cleared #102 (#179)
commitResults.messageBody:
A mistaken email cannot be removed without deleting and re-creating
the student. The edit descriptor also needs to distinguish leaving
an email unchanged from explicitly clearing it.

Let's support edit INDEX -e "" to remove only the email, preserve
other fields, and save and reload the absent value consistently.
Keep replacement and clearing intent explicit in the descriptor.
Update the guides and manual checks to match the behavior.

Fixes #102

Validation: ./gradlew check coverage passes on the branch and with
all three issue branches combined. Tests cover validation, edit
intent, unchanged fields, and JSON save/reload compatibility.

commitResults.messageTitle: TAB-128: Confirm before all data is wiped #143 (#180)
commitResults.messageBody:
Clear deletes all student records immediately, making a mistyped
command capable of wiping the book without warning.

Let's show the whole-book count and require an explicit y/yes reply
before deleting or saving. Accept n/no or an empty reply to cancel,
ignore case and surrounding whitespace, and reject other replies.
Trim replies in linear time and report inconsistent confirmation
state as command feedback. Update the guides and manual checks.

Fixes #143

Validation: ./gradlew check coverage passes on the branch and with
all three issue branches combined. Tests cover exact replies, long
input, hidden records, cancellation without writes, persistence,
and confirmation through the real command line UI.

Align CI with JavaFX 17
commitResults.messageBody:
CI uses the JavaFX bundled with Zulu JDK 25, which differs from the
JavaFX 17.0.7 dependency used by local builds and the release JAR.
This makes UI test results depend on the JDK package.

Let's use the plain JDK package in CI and document the matching
local test and runtime setup.

commitResults.messageTitle: Keep narrow card details inside their row
commitResults.messageBody:
JavaFX 17 can leave a pixel undistributed when shrinking a detail
row. Platform font widths make the email extend outside a narrow
student card on Windows and at nearby widths on Linux.

Let's reserve that pixel, check a range of narrow card widths, and
document the layout constraint and manual verification.

commitResults.messageTitle: Match CI JDK to JavaFX native architecture
commitResults.messageBody:
The macOS runner uses an ARM64 JDK, but the packaged JavaFX native
libraries target x64. UI tests fail during initialization and the
test process stalls after the toolkit fails to start.

Let's select an x64 JDK in CI and document the matching local and
Apple Silicon runtime requirements.

commitResults.messageTitle: Bound CI builds and expose test failure details
commitResults.messageBody:
A native JavaFX startup failure can leave the macOS test process
stalled without an exception trace in the default Gradle output.

Let's report full test failures and stop the build after five
minutes so CI preserves useful diagnostics instead of hanging.

commitResults.messageTitle: Run Mac UI tests on native Intel hardware
commitResults.messageBody:
The bundled JavaFX libraries target Intel Macs. An x64 JDK on the
Apple Silicon runner runs under Rosetta, where UI initialization
is slow and the ten-second test deadline expires.

Let's use a native Intel macOS runner to match the packaged runtime
and document why the runner architecture is explicit.

commitResults.messageTitle: Use the verified x64 Mac CI configuration
commitResults.messageBody:
The native Intel macOS 26 runner stalls during JavaFX startup,
whereas the Apple Silicon runner with an x64 JDK passes the full
suite in the diagnostic run.

Let's retain the passing runner configuration with an explicit x64
JDK and keep the failure diagnostics and build timeout.

commitResults.messageTitle: Allow cold Mac UI initialization in tests
commitResults.messageBody:
Cold window initialization under Rosetta can exceed the UI test
helper's ten-second deadline. The helper times out even though its
callback then completes and the remaining UI tests pass.

Let's allow sixty seconds for JavaFX thread work and document the
deadline. These tests check behavior, not startup performance, and
the complete CI build remains bounded at five minutes.

commitResults.messageTitle: Address CI runtime and diagnostics review
commitResults.messageBody:
The Mac quick start asks users to avoid bundled JavaFX but links
to the course guide that installs it. CI does not cover that setup,
and its build deadline and verbose logs hinder diagnosis.

Let's distinguish the supported runtimes, test the course's native
Mac JDK+FX setup alongside JavaFX 17, allow fifteen minutes for the
build, and print full test failures without verbose Gradle logs.

commitResults.messageTitle: UI tests run on JavaFX 17 locally but JavaFX 25 in CI #174 (#219)
commitResults.messageBody:
CI and local builds use different JavaFX versions, making UI
failures difficult to reproduce. The course's Mac setup also needs
coverage alongside the JavaFX 17 release runtime.

Let's test JavaFX 17 on all three platforms with plain x64 JDKs,
including an x64 JDK under Rosetta on the Apple Silicon Mac runner.
Also test the course's native ARM64 JDK+FX setup on macOS, align
the setup guides, fix narrow-card rounding, allow cold UI startup,
and retain readable failure diagnostics with build-time headroom.

Fixes #174

commitResults.messageTitle: Reuse the shared JavaFX toolkit in UI tests
commitResults.messageBody:
Five UI test classes duplicate toolkit startup and dispatch with a
ten-second timeout. These copies miss the shared helper's cold-start
allowance and implicit-exit handling, risking failures across classes.

Let's delegate startup and dispatch to FxToolkit while preserving the
existing assertions, layout setup and asynchronous settling.

commitResults.messageTitle: Create only displayable student tag labels
commitResults.messageBody:
Tag rows create labels and tooltip listeners for every tag even though
at most three tags can be displayed. Extra labels retain scene nodes
without adding information to the card.

Let's cap label creation while retaining all names for overflow counts
and tooltips, and cover layout and tag-list replacement regressions.

commitResults.messageTitle: Measure help content after the deferred resize
commitResults.messageBody:
The help-window regression test measures the outer window before the
queued re-fit runs. The frame can hide a scene that is too narrow, so
the test can pass while the address or button is clipped on Windows.

Let's measure the scene after a second FX-thread dispatch, check both
content dimensions, and keep the window open until measurement ends.

commitResults.messageTitle: Refit the help window after pulse styling settles
commitResults.messageBody:
The stricter help test exposes a scene two pixels narrower than its
content on Linux. Dispatch alone can run before focus styling and
native window dimensions settle, leaving the content clipped.

Let's re-fit after the first rendering pulse and measure after a pulse
in the regression test. Include manual checks for opening and reopening
the help window across platforms.

commitResults.messageTitle: Show full clipped email addresses on hover
commitResults.messageBody:
Student cards shorten email addresses to fit the details row without
showing the full address on hover. Readers must widen the window or
run another command to recover the value.

Let's add width-aware email tooltips and remove them when the address
fits. Cover narrowing and widening and document the manual checks.

commitResults.messageTitle: Keep help-button focus within its border
commitResults.messageBody:
The global focused-button style adds border insets to the help button.
Its content grows by two pixels after focus arrives, leaving the scene
narrower than the content even once native resizing has settled.

Let's keep the focused border within the button's existing insets and
retain the deferred native-frame fit. Measure after the following pulse
to allow asynchronous resize events to settle.

commitResults.messageTitle: Preserve word boundaries in pasted commands
commitResults.messageBody:
JavaFX removes tabs and line breaks from text-field input. Pasting
spreadsheet cells can therefore silently join name or field values
before the parser receives the command.

Let's convert pasted separators to spaces before JavaFX filters them.
Cover selection replacement, colouring and actual clipboard submission,
and document that pasted text remains a single command.

commitResults.messageTitle: Defer help fitting until native frames arrive
commitResults.messageBody:
A virtual display can report no frame during the first dispatch after
showing the help window. Fitting against those dimensions leaves its
scene two pixels too narrow when the native border arrives.

Let's queue the re-fit after the first rendering pulse so the native
frame is included while preserving the focused-button geometry fix.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add session command-history navigation
commitResults.messageBody:
The command box needs to recall submissions while preserving the draft
that precedes navigation. Treating the draft as another submitted entry
would lose edits or offer unsent text as a historical command.

Let's keep session submissions and the draft separately, skip only
consecutive identical submissions, and test navigation boundaries.

commitResults.messageTitle: Recall submitted commands with Up and Down
commitResults.messageBody:
The command box requires users to retype recent commands, including
rejected input they only need to correct. Its existing colouring and
caret behavior must also follow recalled text.

Let's connect session history to unmodified Up and Down keys, record
submissions before execution, and document draft restoration and
session lifetime. Verify the visible text, caret and colours together.

commitResults.messageTitle: Size the help scene from its styled content
commitResults.messageBody:
On a virtual Linux display the native window width equals the scene
width, yet setting that width can lose two pixels to GTK decorations.
Fixed FXML scene dimensions also prevent sizeToScene from using the
content's preferred size.

Let's let JavaFX size the scene after the deferred fit, remove fixed
scene dimensions, and check content layout at its preferred size.

commitResults.messageTitle: Cover history shortcut modifiers and navigation
commitResults.messageBody:
History shortcuts must leave modified arrows and other editing keys to
the text field. The integration tests cover Shift but leave the other
modifier paths and the ordinary-key fallback untested.

Let's check each modifier and the fallback, and verify that walking
history never submits another command.

commitResults.messageTitle: Pin tooltips for names cut by narrow cards
commitResults.messageBody:
The card already uses width-aware name tooltips, but the reported
short names and real narrow-card widths lack direct regression cases.
The manual guide also focuses on names beyond the character limit.

Let's verify each reported name across narrow widths and after widening,
and document reading short names when a crowded card cuts them.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge master into the help-window branch
commitResults.messageBody:
Master includes email tooltip documentation beside the help-window
notes, leaving the two independent additions in conflict.

Let's preserve both explanations and include the shared toolkit tests
and application assertion checks from master.

commitResults.messageTitle: Clarify pasted spreadsheet spacing in the guide
commitResults.messageBody:
Spreadsheet copies can include a trailing line break. The manual test
promises one space before the phone option even though preserving that
separator and typing a space can produce two.

Let's allow the extra clipboard spacing in the expected result while
still checking that pasted name words remain separate.

commitResults.messageTitle: Keep name-tooltip regressions font independent
commitResults.messageBody:
Windows and macOS fonts can fit the reported short names at wider
card sizes. Requiring every tested width to cut the name rejects
correct layouts on those platforms.

Let's require clipping at the minimum width and otherwise match tooltip
expectations to whether the rendered name is whole. Keep the widening
check that removes the tooltip when all of the name fits.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge master into the tag-label branch
commitResults.messageBody:
Master adds email tooltip documentation alongside the tag-row design
notes and moves UI tests to the shared toolkit helper.

Let's retain both independent explanations and bring the tag-label
regressions onto the same shared toolkit lifecycle.

commitResults.messageTitle: Keep tag counts whole beside readable names
commitResults.messageBody:
The headline reserves room for the name, but its tag-count-only chip
still says N more with an ellipsis. At minimum width that wording can
be clipped, hiding how many tags the card leaves out.

Let's use a compact N tags total when no chip fits and retain N more
when some do. Verify readable name letters, complete counts and hidden
tag tooltips across flag states, tag counts and narrow card widths.

commitResults.messageTitle: Check tag totals independently of count wording
commitResults.messageBody:
The allocation regression pins the old count-only wording, even though
issue #176 replaces it with a compact total to preserve readable names.
That couples label allocation to an independent layout decision.

Let's verify the full numeric total and complete hidden-name tooltip
without prescribing the count-only wording. Check both changes together
as well as the standalone allocation branch.

commitResults.messageTitle: Clarify compact tag-count review expectations
commitResults.messageBody:
The layout sweep derives expected count text from the same condition as
the implementation, and the manual guide does not state the exact text.
The card-layout explanation also interrupts the general UI overview.

Let's add a fixed rendered-count example, give exact manual-test
expectations, and place the card design in its own subsection.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge master into the command-history branch
commitResults.messageBody:
Master includes the merged clipboard, card-layout and help-window
changes. The command-history branch conflicts with the added command-box
tests and manual-testing instructions.

Let's bring the branch up to date and preserve both the clipboard and
history tests and their manual checks.

commitResults.messageTitle: Make command recall skip unchanged and blank input
commitResults.messageBody:
A rejected command remains in the box and in history, so the first Up
shows the same text. Blank clear replies also become invisible history
entries. Both cases make navigation appear unresponsive.

Let's skip the newest entry when it matches the draft and an earlier
entry exists, omit blank submissions, and cover both paths in tests
and the guides.

commitResults.messageTitle: Keep long contact details readable on cards
commitResults.messageBody:
A long annotated phone keeps its preferred width, so the card clips it
mid-number and pushes the email outside the visible area. Readers have
no indication that the number is incomplete.

Let's give each contact its own shrinking line, show an ellipsis for
clipped values, and reveal the full phone on hover. Cover the reported
phones at narrow and default widths and document the card behavior.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge master into the contact-details branch
Wrap card details only when they do not fit
commitResults.messageBody:
Separate detail lines make ordinary cards taller and reduce how many
students fit in the list, even when every field fits on one line.
Long accepted IDs also lack the tooltip available for other contacts.

Let's wrap whole labels only when needed, cap them at the row width,
and reveal every clipped detail on hover. Add compact-height, forced
clipping, resize and overflow regressions, update the guides, and show
the full list before and after the change.

commitResults.messageTitle: Measure card rows by their unwrapped width
commitResults.messageBody:
JavaFX 25 can reserve wrapped rows after widening a card because the
flow pane's preferred wrap length is independent of its content.
The resize regression catches the extra preferred height in CI.

Let's report the natural width of one complete row so parent boxes
measure the height at the allocated width. Keep the strict height
regression and account for pixel rounding when widening in tests.

commitResults.messageTitle: Show command help in the main window
commitResults.messageBody:
Help opens a separate window with only a User Guide link, which
interrupts the CLI workflow and leaves command syntax out of reach.

Let's show all supported commands and common syntax in the main
window, provide keyboard access to the full summary, and keep the
command box ready for the next command. Update the guides and UI
regressions to cover the new help flow and rejected arguments.

commitResults.messageTitle: Use a full-page keyboard pager for help
commitResults.messageBody:
The command summary shares space with the student list and requires
switching focus to read through a short result area. This makes help
awkward to use from the keyboard.

Let's give help the whole content area with familiar pager controls
and a persistent progress prompt. Restore the student view and any
unfinished command when the user quits help, and align the guides
and UI tests with this workflow.

commitResults.messageTitle: Organize the help reference for easier scanning
commitResults.messageBody:
The help reference packs command syntax and usage notes into a dense
block, making it difficult to find a command or distinguish its options.

Let's use consistent command blocks, indented syntax and separate
sections for aliases and input rules. Align the reference in a
monospaced font and separate the pager controls with a divider.

commitResults.messageTitle: Shorten help pager key labels
commitResults.messageBody:
The pager footer spells out long key names and repeats navigation
words, making its controls harder to scan in a narrow window.

Let's use Esc, PgUp and PgDn with compact navigation descriptions,
and keep the guides and help screenshot consistent with the footer.

commitResults.messageTitle: Cover the remaining help pager paths
commitResults.messageBody:
The pager tests leave alternate navigation keys, modified shortcuts
and the fully visible reference case uncovered. These paths affect
whether reading stays predictable at different window sizes.

Let's verify the alternate keys, ignored input, modifier handling
and resizing between fitting and overflowing content so every pager
line and branch is exercised.

commitResults.messageTitle: Keep the help change focused and consistent
commitResults.messageBody:
The PR changes ordinary result scrolling even though help has its
own page, and retains the old window's unused icon. The reference
also uses a different phone placeholder from the User Guide.

Let's restore ordinary result behavior, remove the unused icon and
align the guide with the shared phone label. Shorten reference lines
for narrow windows and include exit in the command summary.

commitResults.messageTitle: Match phone searches with grouping spaces
commitResults.messageBody:
Phone searches ignore punctuation but treat grouping spaces as
literal text. Pasting a number from a roster can therefore miss the
same number stored with different formatting.

Let's include Unicode grouping whitespace in numeric phone searches
while retaining literal annotation matching and all other filters.
Align the guides and cover matching, saved data, and reload behavior.

commitResults.messageTitle: Document safe manual data-file editing
commitResults.messageBody:
The user guide invites direct data-file edits without saying that TAB
loads records only at startup. A reader can lose hand edits when the
running application next saves its in-memory records.

Let's document closing every TAB window, backing up the file, and
restarting after edits. Add a manual check for the safe editing path.

commitResults.messageTitle: Normalize invisible marks in clear replies
commitResults.messageBody:
Clear confirmation bypasses command parsing, so a copied invisible
mark makes a visible yes, no, or empty reply fail. This conflicts
with the command format rules and leaves users guessing why.

Let's apply the shared format-character rule before trimming replies,
retain shaping joiners and internal spaces, and test data preservation
and accepted reply variants. Update the guides and manual checks.

commitResults.messageTitle: Clear tags for quoted whitespace-only values
commitResults.messageBody:

clear tags. The error calls the normalized empty value invalid,
contradicting the documented clearing syntax.

Let's recognize a single empty normalized tag as a request to clear
tags, including Unicode whitespace. Keep mixed blank and nonblank
tags invalid, and verify unchanged details and persisted results.

Let's describe the error, unchanged file, and recovery through a
backup restored while TAB is closed.

commitResults.messageBody:
The product value proposition promises that every change is undoable.
TAB has no undo command, and the guide describes undo and redo only
as a proposed feature, so this promise misrepresents the product.

Let's retain the shipped offline-storage benefit and remove the
unimplemented undo claim from the value proposition.

commitResults.messageBody:

Let's name repeated options and ask for each listed option only once.
Use the shared wording for both kinds of option, retain alias and
validation rules, and verify feedback and state preservation.

commitResults.messageTitle: Clarify follow-up behavior after review
commitResults.messageBody:
The repeated follow-up assertions can look accidental, and the
User Guide leaves the clear option's command scope implicit. The
reason for keeping only a long clear option is also undocumented.

Let's label the repeated requests, state that clearing is edit-only,
and record the alias trade-off for future maintainers.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add -nf alias for clearing follow-up
commitResults.messageBody:
Clearing follow-up requires the long option even though setting it
has a short form, making the opposite action slower to request.

Let's accept -nf as the same clear option as --no-follow-up, cover
its repeated use, persistence, conflicts and duplicates, and align
the command guidance and manual-testing instructions.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add one tag without replacing existing tags
commitResults.messageBody:
Editing tags replaces the entire set, so adding a group to a student
requires re-entering every existing tag and risks losing earlier ones.

Let's add a tag command that preserves the student's other details,
reports existing tags without saving, and documents additive tagging.

commitResults.messageTitle: Cover tag command equality and diagnostics
commitResults.messageBody:
Tag command tests leave equality branches and the diagnostic string
uncovered, causing the PR's patch coverage check to fail.

Let's cover command comparisons, diagnostic output and null inputs.

commitResults.messageTitle: Share required index parsing between commands
commitResults.messageBody:
Edit and tag repeat the checks that distinguish a missing student
index from an invalid one.

Let's share required index validation while keeping each command's
tag rules and error collection in its own parser.

commitResults.messageTitle: Use action flags for adding student tags
commitResults.messageBody:
The tag command marks its tag value with -t, repeating the command's
name without identifying the operation.

Let's use -a and --add for adding a tag so that options identify the
action, and align parsing, tests and user guidance with that syntax.

commitResults.messageTitle: Clarify tag errors and duplicate feedback
commitResults.messageBody:
Negative indexes are reported only as unknown options, and missing
add options give little guidance. Duplicate replies repeat the typed
case even when the stored tag uses another spelling.

Let's explain the index and option errors, guide users toward the add
option, and report duplicate tags using their stored spelling.

commitResults.messageTitle: Derive tag usage text from its option definition
commitResults.messageBody:
Tag usage repeats the add option's spellings separately from the flag
definition, so a future change can leave the help text out of sync.

Let's derive the option label, aliases, example and add guidance from
FLAG_ADD_TAG, consistently with the other command usage messages.

commitResults.messageTitle: Make Student optional details explicit
commitResults.messageBody:
Student stores absent email, NUS Student ID, and follow-up details as
null. Constructors hide absence, and callers unwrap optional values
back into null before construction.

Let's use explicit optionals throughout Student and its construction
callers, remove null-supplying overloads, and preserve the existing
JSON and display contracts. Cover the migrated boundary and clearing
round trip with regression tests, and document the model contract.

Fixes #181
Fixes #208

commitResults.messageTitle: Support removing a single student tag
commitResults.messageBody:
The tag command adds one tag, but removing a group still requires
replacing the student's entire tag set. This risks losing unrelated
groups when a teaching assistant removes just one membership.

Let's extend tag with a removal action that preserves other details,
reports absent tags without saving, and shares the existing parsing
and persistence paths. Cover normalized matching and failures with
regression tests, and document removal and its manual test path.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge master into optional details branch
commitResults.messageBody:
Master adds TagCommand with the previous nullable Student construction
contract, so combining the branches fails to compile.

Let's bring in master, pass TagCommand's optionals directly, and pin
the distinction between students who both have no NUS Student ID.

commitResults.messageTitle: Wait for Help-window sizing assertions to pass
commitResults.messageBody:
Help-window tests assume native resizing finishes within two pulses.
A window that fits a later pulse therefore fails the full check even
though its deferred fit works.

Let's retry both sizing assertions until they pass or the shared timeout
expires, preserve the last failure for diagnostics, and cover polling
success, timeout cleanup and unexpected exceptions.

commitResults.messageTitle: Tag command: Complete equality contract
commitResults.messageBody:
TagCommand compares its action but inherits Object's hash code. Equal
commands can therefore behave differently in hashed collections. Its
addition result also retains a generic success name after removal adds a
separate counterpart.

Let's hash every equality field and name the addition success message
explicitly.

commitResults.messageTitle: Align command tests with their evidence
commitResults.messageBody:
The requirement tests describe keyboard-only and offline behavior
while exercising command dispatch and local persistence. Hash tests
also require distinct results to have distinct hashes, exceeding
the equality contract.

Let's name the integration tests for the behavior they establish
and check equal-result hash consistency across both constructors.
Retain the dispatch, persistence and field-sensitive equality checks.

commitResults.messageTitle: Keep startup working when log files cannot open
commitResults.messageBody:
LogsCenter reports file-handler failures through a logger that is
not initialized yet. Starting TAB from a read-only folder therefore
crashes before the UI opens instead of retaining console logging.

Let's report the failure through the configured base logger and
continue without a file handler. Cover first-use failures in fresh
JVMs and document folder permissions and the manual startup check.

commitResults.messageTitle: Recover from null GUI settings at startup
commitResults.messageBody:
An explicit null guiSettings value bypasses the UserPrefs setter
during JSON loading. Startup writes that invalid preference back
before the model rejects it, so every later launch fails as well.

Let's reject null GUI settings at the storage boundary so the
existing startup recovery restores and saves defaults. Cover file
repair and repeated initialization without changing student data,
and document the recovery behavior and manual verification.

commitResults.messageTitle: Record coverage from logging subprocesses
commitResults.messageBody:
The logging probes exercise file-handler failures in fresh JVMs,
but those processes do not run the parent's JaCoCo agent. The
warning therefore appears uncovered even when its regression passes.

Let's include the probes in the same coverage report while keeping
their startup isolation and existing assertions.

commitResults.messageTitle: Restore tag test selection after restart
commitResults.messageBody:
The removal manual tests restart TAB before another indexed command.
Restarting clears the filter, so index 1 can select another student.

Let's restore the Tag Test search after each restart before removing
the next tag, and confirm that only the intended student is shown.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge master into the tag removal branch
commitResults.messageBody:
Master requires explicit optional student details and provides an
in-app command reference. The tag removal branch needs both contracts
to remain complete when integrated.

Let's retain tag removal with the optional constructor arguments,
preserve both guides, and cover removal in the command reference.

commitResults.messageTitle: Save only when commands change student records
commitResults.messageBody:
Every completed command saves the student book, so an unwritable data
folder makes list and exit fail even though they change no records.
The save error also prevents the exit request from reaching the UI.

Let's save only when a command changes the student records, keep
read-only commands usable after a failed save, and document and test
the behavior in unwritable folders.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge master into 198-fix-read-only-folder-startup
commitResults.messageBody:
Master adds a help pager beside the read-only-folder manual test,
which conflicts with this branch's guide additions.

Let's retain both test paths and align the read-only instructions
with the help pager's quit keys.

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject null JSON documents during startup
commitResults.messageBody:
A preferences file containing only null bypasses GUI validation and
stops startup before recovery can run. A null student document fails
at the same point, and preference warnings omit the failure reason.

Let's reject null documents through the existing data-loading error
paths, preserve invalid student data for repair, and include the
reason when restoring preferences. Cover both storage readers and
startup recovery, and update the guides and manual testing steps.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge master into 199-recover-null-gui-settings
commitResults.messageBody:
Master adds storage logging documentation beside the preference
recovery explanation, which prevents this branch from merging cleanly.

Let's retain both storage explanations and bring the branch up to date
with the team's latest changes.

commitResults.messageTitle: Detect elided counts in the summary panel test
commitResults.messageBody:
The summary test uses a wider panel and a single-digit count, so it
cannot detect a count squeezed by a long tag at the app's width.

Let's exercise a two-digit count at 150 pixels and assert the drawn
text and available width rather than the minimum-width setting.

commitResults.messageTitle: Show complete tag names in the summary panel
commitResults.messageBody:
Long sidebar tags lose their endings, making tags with a shared
prefix look identical and hiding which tag belongs to each count.

Let's wrap complete tag names beside their counts and document the
scrolling behavior so readers can distinguish them without hovering.

commitResults.messageTitle: Read UTF-8 data without silent character loss
commitResults.messageBody:
A leading UTF-8 BOM prevents valid JSON from loading, while malformed
UTF-8 is silently decoded into replacement characters that can later
be saved over the user's letters.

Let's accept a leading BOM, reject malformed UTF-8 with recovery
guidance, and preserve unreadable files through startup and shutdown.

commitResults.messageTitle: Warn concisely when preferences cannot be saved
commitResults.messageBody:
Recoverable preference writes print exception traces, and shutdown
labels the failure severe even though the session remains usable.

Let's warn once with the path, reason and effect on preferences at
startup and shutdown, retaining session settings without a trace.

commitResults.messageTitle: Guard the sidebar count test's layout conditions
commitResults.messageBody:
The count test can pass without squeezing the labels when font metrics
change, or when an oversized row moves the count outside the viewport.

Let's assert the space pressure and visible row bounds, and import
Text alongside the other JavaFX types as suggested in review.

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject unknown student data keys before saving
commitResults.messageBody:
Misspelled JSON keys load without warning and disappear on an unrelated
save, losing values entered by hand. Legacy address fields and file
comments still need to load for compatibility.

Let's reject unsupported student and book keys with a clear diagnostic,
preserve the compatibility exceptions, and verify recovery without data
loss in tests and guides.

commitResults.messageTitle: Cover display ordering during window restoration
commitResults.messageBody:
Secondary-screen ordering depends on the runner's connected displays,
so single-screen CI leaves that branch untested.

Let's separate primary-display ordering from native screen discovery
and verify secondary positions, primary fallback and unchanged inputs.

commitResults.messageTitle: Cover unknown fields in unnamed student records
commitResults.messageBody:
Unknown fields in records without a name use a separate diagnostic
that the storage regressions do not exercise.

Let's verify the exact error for missing and null names and ensure the
rejected file remains unchanged.

commitResults.messageTitle: Show UI highlighting and control inheritance
commitResults.messageBody:
The UI class diagram omits the highlighter used by CommandBox and
leaves the custom card controls disconnected from their JavaFX base
classes. This obscures the distinction between UiPart controllers
and controls declared in the card layout.

Let's show the highlighting dependency and direct JavaFX inheritance,
explain these relationships beside the diagram, and include its
rendered preview.

commitResults.messageTitle: Clarify window restoration rules
commitResults.messageBody:
Window restoration has no explicit regression for equal overlaps or
windows spanning adjacent displays. Its method name and description
also omit the restored position and adjusted minimum dimensions.

Let's document and test the placement rules, describe the method's
full purpose, and keep screenshots in the existing evidence folder.

commitResults.messageTitle: Identify student records in JSON load errors
commitResults.messageBody:
Unknown-key errors name the student but leave records ambiguous when
names are absent or shared. The address compatibility comment also
attributes older TAB data files to AB3.

Let's add the record number to student mapping errors, cover ambiguous
records without changing file bytes, and clarify the guides and comment.

commitResults.messageTitle: Shorten the UI diagram inheritance connector
commitResults.messageBody:
The CommandTextField inheritance connector loops around the Model box,
which makes the TextField relationship harder to follow. The diagram
preview also sits beside sources even though the guide renders PlantUML.

Let's guide Model to the right of StudentCard for a direct inheritance
connector and keep the regenerated preview in the PR evidence folder.

commitResults.messageTitle: Simplify student mapping path lookup
commitResults.messageBody:
The mapping wrapper checks path shapes that the student-book schema
cannot produce, leaving unreachable branches in the coverage gate.

Let's use the first array index in the mapping path to identify the
student record while retaining the existing diagnostics.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add matching rules for student fields
commitResults.messageBody:
General searches cannot restrict a term to one student field. Let's add
field matchers and tests while preserving the existing general-search
callers for the parser transition.

commitResults.messageTitle: Parse field selectors in find commands
commitResults.messageBody:
General search cannot exclude matches from unrelated fields. Let's
accept the existing field option aliases, repeated conditions and quoted
phrases, and describe field selectors in command help.

commitResults.messageTitle: Migrate search tests to explicit fields
commitResults.messageBody:
Field selectors let tests state which student detail a search exercises.
Let's migrate the existing command fixtures and integration searches to
explicit fields while checking AND matching and unchanged storage.

commitResults.messageTitle: Document field selectors in the User Guide
commitResults.messageBody:
Search examples rely on general matching and omit field selectors. Let's
document the field options and migrate the worked commands to explicit
fields so their parser checks remain useful.

commitResults.messageTitle: Update field-search design and manual tests
commitResults.messageBody:
The Developer Guide describes general matching and its manual commands
omit field selectors. Let's migrate those find examples to field
selectors and describe matching within fields and repeated tag
conditions.

commitResults.messageTitle: Require field options for search terms
commitResults.messageBody:
Bare terms make a search's field implicit. Let's require an option for
every term, report bare values clearly, and remove the general-search
compatibility helpers after migrating their callers.

commitResults.messageTitle: Match an optional follow-up search state
commitResults.messageBody:
Field terms cannot select students by their follow-up status. Let's
allow the predicate to require either status alone or together with
field terms, and test both states without changing the default search
behavior.

commitResults.messageTitle: Find students by follow-up status
commitResults.messageBody:
Field selectors leave no way to list students by follow-up status. Let's
support -f and -nf with their existing long aliases, alone or combined
with field terms, and document and test conflicts, duplicates and
unchanged storage.

commitResults.messageTitle: Clarify find feedback and matching
commitResults.messageBody:
Find's unexpected-value hint suggests a bare first term even though
all search terms require a field option. Follow-up conflict messages
and help spellings also duplicate the shared flag definitions, while
the predicate combines several matching decisions in one expression.

Let's clarify the hint, share conflict feedback, derive the help from
flag definitions and name each matching decision. Extend rejection
checks to preserve results and saved data for common typing mistakes.

commitResults.messageTitle: Align search documentation with field options
commitResults.messageBody:
The general search story can suggest searching across all fields, and
an unused screenshot depicts syntax that field selectors replace.

Let's clarify that the user chooses the search field and remove the
obsolete screenshot while preserving the story priorities.

commitResults.messageTitle: Restore positional value guidance
commitResults.messageBody:
The shared unexpected-value message omits the hint that a command's
name or index belongs before its options. Users of add, edit and tag
lose guidance for correcting a misplaced value.

Let's restore that hint with wording that applies only when the
command takes a name or index without an option, so it also stays
accurate for find's mandatory field options.
